title: crumbkit/self-usage/v1
description: The patterns in the usage log where callers waste effort, and a summary of the runs read.

data.description: The rows of the page, up to the limit.

total.description: The number of rows that matched, of which data holds one page.

caller.description: The coding agent's id, such as claude-code, person or unknown.

CommandFigures.description: The figures of one command since the start of the report.

help_before.description:
The help pages that each run's session read since its last run
that printed no help page, summed over the runs.

help_pages.description: The runs that printed the command's help page.

p95_ms.description:
The 95th percentile of the runs' wall time in milliseconds, or null
when every run printed help.

p95_out_bytes.description:
The 95th percentile of the bytes that the runs wrote to standard
output, or null when no run printed a result.

refused.description: The runs whose command line was refused.

runs.description: The runs that did not print a help page.

FindingRow.description:
One finding of `self usage`: a pattern in the runs of one command that
suggests where callers waste effort.

code.description:
The code of the failure that the runs retried, for a retry after
failure only.

command.description:
The command path below the tool's name, such as `books show`, or the
tool's name for its root command.

figures.description: The figures of the command since the start of the report.

runs.description: The runs that show the pattern.

suggestion.description: What the pattern suggests, or the figure that raised it.

Kind.description:
The kinds of finding, with the runs that each one counts. Each kind
serializes as the name that `self usage` prints, such as
`one id at a time`.

oneOf.description:
A session ran a command that takes many ids with one id at least 3
times within 2 minutes. It counts those runs.

A session ran the same command line again within 60 seconds. It
counts the repeats.

A session read at least 3 help pages before its first successful
run, or without one. It counts the pages, under the command of the
last page.
The parser refused the command line. It counts the refused runs.

A session ran a command again within 60 seconds of its failure. It
counts the retries, under the code of the failure.

A session followed a cut-short listing within 60 seconds with the
same command and `--all` or `--limit`. It counts those runs. The
record holds no limit value, so any `--limit` counts, also one that
asks for fewer rows than the default page.

The 95th percentile of a command's output is at least 20,000 bytes.
It counts the runs that wrote that much.

The 95th percentile of a command's wall time is at least 1 second.
It counts the runs that took that long.

UsageSummary.description:
The summary of the runs that `self usage` read. The text output prints
it as one line above the table, such as `1,284 runs in 23 sessions since
30 Sep: claude-code 1,201, person 83.`

callers.description: The runs of each caller, the most first.

runs.description: The runs that the report read.

sessions.description: The sessions that the runs came from.

since.description: The day in UTC on which the report starts, such as 2026-09-30.

skipped.description:
The records that the report left out, because they named a command,
flag, code or caller that the tool does not write.
